I farm here in the North West, and this maize plot is small but it feeds my household so I must manage it well. Rain comes when it comes, so I cannot irrigate — I will plant with the first good rains and intercrop with cowpea as I always do. Fertilizer is expensive but without urea and NPK the maize will not give good cobs, so I will buy what I can afford, maybe one bag of NPK and one of urea for this plot. I will use improved seed from the agro-dealer because the armyworm trouble has been bad, and I will spray when I see the worms in the funnel. My wife and older children help me, so most of the work is family labor, but at weeding and harvest I hire a few young men from the village for a day or two.
